The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control has uncovered suspected tramadol hydrochloride powder concealed in a 40-foot container declared as corn starch at the Apapa Port in Lagos. The agency disclosed this in a post on its official X handle on Wednesday, saying its Port Inspection Directorate acted on intelligence. “During examination, officers discovered bags labelled ‘Tramadol Hydrochloride’ concealed within outer bags marked ‘Corn Starch’, raising concerns about possible misdeclaration and concealment,” NAFDAC said. It added, “The consignment also had no evidence of the requisite NAFDAC permits or payment receipt at the time of examination.” According to the agency, samples of the suspected substance have been collected and sent for laboratory analysis. The container remains in the custody of the Nigeria Customs Service, Apapa Command, pending the laboratory findings and further regulatory action. The agency did not disclose the quantity or value of the consignment, the identity of the importer, its country of origin, or whether any arrests had been made. The latest discovery comes amid a series of enforcement operations by the agency, mostly in Lagos. PUNCH Online reports that a NAFDAC enforcement operation uncovered unlabelled and unregistered cosmetics and packaging materials at the Tools and Hardware Complex, Trade Fair Complex, Ojo. The raid followed an earlier operation in February, during which the agency said it seized banned and counterfeit cosmetics worth over ₦3bn in the same market. Faith Alofe
